summary: Exceptionally strong Phase 1 candidate. The rendered Nord Stage 4 73 surface reproduces the measured reference geometry almost exactly (chassis aspect 3.0951 vs registry 3.0951; 0.94 viewport width fraction; 54/46 deck/keybed split; 13/21/15/9/21/21 section widths verified in live DOM), with a complete, reference-specific six-section hardware inventory (150 panel controls + 73-key E1-E7 keybed, nine LED-laddered drawbars, exactly two OLEDs in Program and Synth, eight Program buttons matching the reference photo). Behavior was verified directly in Chromium: pointer, independent three-point multi-touch, mapped computer keyboard with repeat suppression, and truthful MIDI-denied handling all feed one note lifecycle; analyser taps on the single lazily-created AudioContext confirmed audible output, monotonic velocity response (soft peak RMS 0.107 vs hard 0.294), sustain hold/release, 24-voice deterministic stealing, and silence after blur/release. The decorative boundary is honest and proven: operating knobs/buttons/drawbars before any key press created zero AudioContexts, and the status strip explicitly declares panel controls visual-only and the voice as generated synthesis with no samples. All four technical checks pass (113/113 tests) and a rebuild reproduces the sealed dist byte-for-byte. Remaining gaps are cosmetic: ~10 legend strings ellipsis-truncated at 1440x900 (e.g. Synth OLED 'Super S…', Delay 'EFFECTS: CHOR · VIBE · ENS · FLAM · SPAC…'), sub-pixel illegible legends at 390x844 (structure fully retained, nothing clipped), simplified micro-detail, and a ~200-500ms first-note warm-up latency while the AudioContext starts.

criteria.label: Silhouette, chassis, and geometry
evidence: Measured live at 1440x900: instrument box 1353.6x437.3px at x=43.2/y=219.8, aspect ratio 3.0951 matching the variant registry's measured 3.0951 exactly; width fraction 0.940 within the required 0.88-0.97; no horizontal or vertical document scroll (scrollWidth/Height 1440/900).
Deck/keybed split verified in DOM as inline 54%/46% heights; six [data-section] widths measured 171.0/276.2/197.3/118.3/276.2/276.2px = exactly 13/21/15/9/21/21% of the deck, in the correct order.

Keybed: 73 [data-midi] key elements, MIDI 28-100 (E1-E7), 43 white/30 black, black-key height ~61% of white (black key h=114.7 vs white 188.1px), correct E-start octave pattern confirmed in a 2x close-up; keys sit inside the continuous chassis between rendered end cheeks with connected top/bottom rails; single red chassis element, no detached frame, no marketing hero, zero elements.

criteria.label: Complete hardware inventory and placement
evidence: 2x close-ups of all six sections compared against crops of reference/nord-stage-4-73.jpg: Performance shows Master Level knob, wooden pitch stick, segmented mod wheel, nord stage 4 / HAMMER ACTION 73 branding, and the Rotary Speaker strip (ON, Drive knob, Organ, Close Mic, Stop Mode, Angle, Slow/Fast with green LED, Morph) matching the photo's landmark set.

Organ: nine physical drawbars with red LED ladders and footage legends (16' ... 1'), organ model group (B3/Vox/Farf/Pipe1/Pipe2/B3 Bass), Vib/Chorus, B3 Percussion (Volume/Decay/Harmonic), two green-LED level faders, Preset/Sync, Octave Shift, KB Zone - all present as on the reference. Piano: layer faders, Acoustics (Soft Rel/String Res), Ped Noise, KB Touch, Dyn Comp, Unison, Timbre rocker, Piano Select with six type LEDs (Grand/Upright/Electric/Clav/Digital/Misc), Info and Model dial. Program: Morph Assign, Split, MST CLK, Transp/Panic, Store/Store As, Preset Library, primary OLED (contents 'A:11 Nord Stage 4 / B3 Soulful / White Grand / Vista Pad Whl' matching the reference photo), large Program encoder, Page/Cat, Live Mode, Layer Scene II, eight numbered Program buttons with secondary legends. Synth: second OLED, three display encoders, Mode/Arpeggiator/Voice/Vibrato/LFO/Oscillators/Filter/Amp/Unison groups, three layer faders. Effects: FX Focus column, Mod 1, Mod 2, Amp Sim/EQ (5 knobs), Delay with Tap/Set + Analog, Comp, Reverb.

Exactly 2 primary OLED displays in the DOM, both inside [data-section=program] and [data-section=synth]; no OLED in Organ/Piano/Performance/Effects (forbidden-landmark check passed). Candidate audit's automated bounds check (150 controls + 73 keys inside owning sections, no overlaps) is consistent with my screenshots; role inventory: 49 sliders, 174 buttons, 0 controls missing accessible names.

Deviation noted and accepted: visual spec lists 'five live-program buttons' but the reference photo and manual show eight numbered Program buttons plus Live Mode; the candidate followed the reference/manual (which the protocol makes authoritative) and documented the conflict in its audit.

criteria.label: Materials, color, typography, and displays
evidence: Red metal chassis with subtle gradient, dark inset plates with red perimeter (matching the spec's panelBlueGray #3c424d and the rubric/BENCHMARK 'dark inset panels' description; note the product photo's plates read lighter blue-gray), black indexed knobs with position marks, red/green LED ladders, lit green LEDs, blue-green OLEDs with authentic reference content, white condensed uppercase legends, tan wooden pitch stick - the material family reads as a credible Stage 4 product study at 1440x900.

Defect: at 1440x900 a truncation survey found ~10 legends ellipsis-truncated, e.g. Synth 'RATE/TIME', 'PATTERN ▿', 'RANGE ENV', Delay 'EFFECTS: CHOR · VIBE · ENS · FLAM · SPAC…', Reverb 'ROOM · STAGE · BOOTH · HALL · SPRING · C…'; the Synth OLED itself renders 'OSC WAVE…' / 'Super S…' where the reference shows 'OSC WAVEFORM' / 'Super Saw'. The candidate audit claimed the Synth OLED truncation was repaired but it is still visible in the sealed build.

Candidate-admitted simplifications confirmed by close-up: no screw heads/brushed texture, approximated Nord logotype, drawbar cap colors follow Hammond convention rather than the photo's mixed tones. These are micro-detail level and do not break the hierarchy.

criteria.label: Narrow retention
evidence: At 390x844 (deviceScaleFactor 2, touch context): no document scroll (390/844 exactly); chassis 378.3x122.2px, width fraction 0.970, aspect 3.0952 preserved; all 73 keys report positive on-screen bounds (73/73 visible); all six sections rendered in order with widths still at 13/21/15/9/21/21% (47.8/77.2/55.1/33.1/77.2/77.2px); status strip legible below the instrument.

Interaction retained at narrow: touchscreen tap on key MIDI 60 at the scaled keybed created the AudioContext (state 'running'); status strip updated to 'Basic piano voice ready (generated synthesis — no samples)'; zero console messages or page errors at this viewport.

Limitation: the whole instrument is scaled to fit 390px, so panel legends are sub-pixel and illegible and keys are only ~8.5px wide; nothing is clipped or lost (candidate audit admits this), but 'legible state' is only partially met at narrow.

criteria.label: Unified playable inputs
evidence: Pointer: mouse press on key MIDI 89 and MIDI 60 (bottom of key, e.g. x=1179/y=606 at 1440x900) created one AudioContext (state 'running'), produced non-silent output through an injected analyser tap before the destination (RMS 0.086-0.29 held, 0 after release), and set data-pressed/aria-pressed true.

Multi-touch: three independent CDP touch points on C4/E4/G4 pressed all three keys ([data-pressed=true] for 60/64/67, RMS 0.274); ending only touch id 2 released only E4 (60/67 remained pressed, RMS 0.140); ending the rest returned RMS to 0. Independent pointer ownership works.

Computer keyboard: physical 'a'/'f'/'d' KeyA-row mapping plays notes (first down started exactly 4 oscillators = 1 voice); 5 synthetic repeated keydowns while held added 0 new voices (repeat suppression); window blur while holding released all voices (RMS 0, 0 pressed keys). Focused-key Enter also plays (aria-label 'E4 key', RMS 0.217) and keyboard note input is sensibly suppressed while focus is on a panel slider/button.

MIDI: headless Chromium genuinely rejects requestMIDIAccess (probed directly: NotAllowedError), and the app's status strip truthfully reported 'MIDI permission denied — keyboard, pointer and touch input still work'; connected/no-device/hot-plug/disconnect-cleanup paths are implemented in src/input/midi.ts (velocity-0 note-off, CC64 sustain, onstatechange port refresh, disconnect all-notes-off) and covered by injected-boundary tests in src/input/midi.test.ts (all passing). All four sources route through one InstrumentController.noteOn/noteOff/setSustain lifecycle with per-source note ownership (src/input/controller.ts).

criteria.label: Voice lifecycle and performance
evidence: Velocity: pointer press at key top vs bottom produced peak RMS 0.107 vs 0.294 (harder-louder, monotonic); engine maps velocity 0.04+0.32*v^1.5 and a fake-boundary test asserts monotonicity across 0.1/0.5/1.0.

Sustain: with Space held, pressing and releasing a key left an audible tail (RMS 0.099 at 600ms after key-up); releasing Space silenced it (RMS 0 after 900ms). Engine semantics verified in source and tests: keys still held during pedal-up keep sounding; sustain pressed after a release does not resurrect the note.

Polyphony/stealing: 30 rapid sustained notes started 120 oscillators (4 partials/voice) with the 24-voice cap enforced by deterministic oldest-first stealing (src/audio/engine.ts releaseVoice of lowest seq; test proves the same voice is stolen on identical sequences); rapid 30-note mash x3 left the app stable, RMS returned to 0, exactly 1 AudioContext alive, zero console errors.

Cleanup: window blur released all held voices and visual key state instantly; releaseVoice cancels scheduled values, stops oscillators, and a timer-driven cleanupVoice disconnects every owned node; the fake-boundary test 'cleans every stolen and released voice back to a stable node count' asserts live nodes <= 2 (master gain + compressor) and 0 pending timers after all-notes-off; unmount dispose() closes the context.

Panel controls stayed decorative during playback: clicking Panic/section buttons and zeroing Master Level while a key sounded did not stop oscillators or change the master gain node (candidate test verified, and my live pass confirmed no audible change path exists - panel interactions never touch the graph).

Minor: the very first note after page load is delayed ~200-500ms while the lazily-created AudioContext spins up (fresh-page sampling: keyboard first note audible at ~500ms, pointer at ~200-250ms); all subsequent notes sound immediately.

criteria.label: Basic source and status honesty
evidence: A dependable audible piano-like voice exists: 4 detuned oscillator partials (triangle+sines) through a velocity/pitch-keyed lowpass and percussive decay envelope into master gain -> DynamicsCompressor limiter -> single destination; verified audible via analyser tap at multiple velocities, notes, and input sources across many page loads with zero failures.

Honesty is explicit end-to-end: status strip shows 'Basic piano voice ready (generated synthesis — no samples)' plus 'Panel controls are visual-only in this phase'; IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS.json declares generated live synthesis, empty sampleSources, and 'No recorded, downloaded, or bundled audio samples are used or claimed'; no sample claims anywhere in the artifact.

Status lifecycle is truthful: idle 'Audio starts on the first key press' -> loading -> ready observed live; error path on context-creation failure and a reduced-graph fallback status ('Running on a reduced audio path (no limiter)') exist in src/audio/engine.ts and are exercised by src/audio/status-cleanup.test.ts; MIDI denied state reported truthfully in headless Chromium.

criteria.label: Control movement and feedback
evidence: Live at 1440x900: Master Level knob (aria-label 'Master Level') moved by pointer drag 64->106 and by ArrowDown keys 106->98; visible 2px blue focus outline when focused. Six sampled aria-pressed buttons (Rotary Organ Source, Rotary Stop Mode, Rotary Speed Slow Fast, Organ Section On, Organ Layer A/B On/Off) all toggled false->true on real clicks with lit state.

Keys visibly depress (data-pressed/aria-pressed observed true during pointer, touch, Enter, and computer-key presses). Candidate tests additionally prove drawbar 0-8 travel with correct pull-down-to-increase drag direction, fader/wheel keyboard movement, Home/End bounds, and the spring-loaded pitch stick returning to 0 on release - all passing in my run of the suite.

Accessible state audit: 49 role=slider controls with aria-valuemin/max/now, 174 buttons, 0 elements missing an accessible name; every rendered panel control carries data-decorative=true and a stable data-control-id from the normalized hardware model (src/model/hardware.ts).

criteria.label: Decorative-control boundary
evidence: Direct proof on a fresh page before any key press: dragging the Master Level knob, arrow-keying it, and clicking latching buttons created zero AudioContexts (hooked constructor count stayed 0). Only a keybed gesture created the context.

While a note sounded, Panic/section toggles/Master Level Home had no effect on the audio graph (oscillator count and master gain node unchanged - candidate test, re-run and passing; consistent with source: panel controls write only to PresentationStore, which has no engine reference).

No false claims: the status strip states 'Panel controls are visual-only in this phase'; the Program OLED does not react to Program buttons/Store/dial (tested); IMPLEMENTATION_DETAILS and the visual audit describe the Panic button as decorative with cleanup only via internal blur/disconnect/unmount paths, which I verified behave exactly that way.

criteria.label: Data structure and tests
evidence: Clean layering: src/model (typed hardware/key data with stable IDs, variant registry), src/audio (engine + injectable AudioBoundary), src/input (controller unifying all sources, MIDI manager, keymap), src/state (PresentationStore for decorative state), src/components (sections/keybed/controls). All browser boundaries (AudioContext factory, timers, MIDI access) are injected; App accepts audioBoundary/midiBoundary props.

113 tests in 13 files, all passing in my clean-room run; the feature matrix maps all 10 required Phase 1 feature IDs to real test files. Tests are meaningful, not smoke: deterministic voice stealing re-runs identical sequences, node/timer counts return to a stable baseline after cleanup, decorative honesty asserts no AudioContext is even created by panel interaction, MIDI tests cover velocity-0, CC64, hot-plug, disconnect and denied, keybed tests cover pointer cancel/lost-capture and multi-touch ownership.

Maintainable React/TypeScript: useSyncExternalStore subscriptions, memoized per-key components, per-pointer note ownership map, no console noise, and a truthful IMPLEMENTATION_PLAN.md/audit trail. Main body of section markup is a single 1068-line sections.tsx - dense but organized per section and acceptable at this scale.

criteria.label: Runtime quality
evidence: Technical gate verified in a pristine copy (Node 24, pnpm 11.7.0 per packageManager, frozen lockfile): pnpm test 113/113 passed, pnpm typecheck clean, pnpm lint exit 0, pnpm build succeeded - and the rebuild reproduced the sealed dist assets byte-identically (index-8lGJlWjV.js / index-D4zflrDh.css match the served preview).

Zero console messages and zero page errors across every one of my Chromium passes (load, full interaction, multi-touch, 30-note mashes, narrow viewport); matches the parent capture's empty console log.

Stability: exactly one AudioContext across a long session; repeated rapid interaction left RMS at 0 and no stuck voices/pressed keys; blur, MIDI-disconnect and unmount cleanup paths implemented and tested; StrictMode-safe lazy restart documented in engine.dispose(). Only quirk: ~200-500ms first-note warm-up latency on the initial gesture.

The candidate audit claimed the OLED truncation was repaired in pass 1, but it persists in the sealed build.

Candidate audit acknowledges this deviation.

All subsequent notes sound immediately. Status honestly reports 'Audio starts on the first key press', so this is a small UX quirk rather than a defect in honesty.
